step: Employer files for Labour Residence Authorization (Autorização de Residência para fins de Trabalho) from MJSP
authority: Ministério da Justiça e Segurança Pública (MJSP) – Coordenação-Geral de Imigração Laboral (CGIL)
form_name: Requerimento de Autorização de Residência para fins de Trabalho
field_label: Employer CNPJ, employee passport copy, proof of professional qualification, employment offer letter, evidence of employer registration on MJSP portal
deadline_label: File at least 60–90 days before intended start date; statutory CGIL processing target is 30 days after receipt of complete dossier
non_obvious_official_guidance: Lei de Migração 13.445/2017 Art. 14 §1 I and Decreto 9.199/2017 require employers to obtain prior authorization from MJSP before a foreign national can apply for a VITEM V work visa at a Brazilian consulate abroad.
non_obvious_actual_reality: Authorization is filed exclusively by the Brazilian employer, not the employee. Many HR teams discover only after the job offer is signed that the employer must be the petitioner and that the online MJSP portal requires a registered CNPJ representative. Without the Autorização de Residência number the employee's consulate appointment cannot proceed.
non_obvious_action_required: Engage a Brazilian immigration lawyer as soon as the hire decision is made. The lawyer registers the employer on the MJSP portal, prepares and files the Requerimento, and tracks approval. Do not schedule the employee's consulate visa appointment until the Autorização de Residência letter is in hand.
source: MJSP – Lei de Migração e autorizações de residência para fins de trabalho

step: Employee applies for VITEM V work visa at Brazilian consulate in country of origin
authority: Ministério das Relações Exteriores (MRE) – Brazilian Consulate in country of origin
form_name: Formulário de Requerimento de Visto (VITEM V – consulate-specific form)
field_label: Valid passport (minimum 6 months validity beyond intended stay), MJSP Labour Authorization number, signed employment contract, proof of professional qualifications, passport photos, consular fee receipt
deadline_label: Apply after MJSP authorization is issued; allow 15–30 business days for consulate processing; book appointment immediately on receiving the authorization
non_obvious_official_guidance: Decreto 9.199/2017 Art. 37 establishes VITEM V (Visto de Residência Temporária para fins de trabalho) as valid for up to 2 years and renewable once within Brazil. The visa grants the right to enter and reside for work but must be converted to an RNM registration at the Polícia Federal within 90 days of arrival.
non_obvious_actual_reality: Processing time varies significantly by consulate: some posts process VITEM V in 5 business days; others take 6+ weeks. The VITEM V is an entry visa, not a work permit — the CRNM registration with the Polícia Federal is the actual residence authorization in Brazil. Employees who arrive and do not register within 90 days become irregular migrants even if their passport visa stamp has not expired.
non_obvious_action_required: Check the specific consulate's current processing schedule and required document list before booking. Book the appointment the same day the MJSP authorization arrives. Confirm whether the consulate requires originals, certified copies, or sworn Portuguese translations of supporting documents — requirements vary by post.

step: Employee pre-registers for CPF (Cadastro de Pessoas Físicas) at Brazilian consulate before departure
authority: Receita Federal do Brasil – via Brazilian consulate or embassy abroad
form_name: Solicitação de inscrição no CPF para residente no exterior
field_label: Valid passport, proof of address in home country, MJSP Labour Authorization number (recommended)
deadline_label: Ideally at or before the visa appointment; strongly recommended before departure to avoid first-month bottlenecks in Brazil
non_obvious_official_guidance: Instrução Normativa RFB 1.880/2019 extended the option for non-residents to register for a CPF through Brazilian consulates and embassies abroad, enabling foreign nationals to obtain a CPF before arriving in Brazil.
non_obvious_actual_reality: Without a CPF the employee cannot open a Brazilian bank account, sign a residential lease, be enrolled in the employer's e-Social payroll system, or obtain a SIM card from most carriers. Many employees arrive assuming the CPF is quickly obtained in Brazil and lose 2–4 weeks waiting for in-country processing. Not all Brazilian consulates have activated the CPF registration service — confirm availability with the specific post before the appointment.
non_obvious_action_required: At the visa appointment ask consulate staff whether CPF registration is available at that post. If yes, request the CPF form and complete it in the same appointment. If the consulate does not offer the service, prioritize CPF registration at a Correios branch, Banco do Brasil, or Caixa Econômica Federal in the first week after arrival.
source: Receita Federal do Brasil – CPF para residentes no exterior

step: Dependants apply for VITEM V dependent visa at Brazilian consulate
authority: Ministério das Relações Exteriores (MRE) – Brazilian Consulate
form_name: Formulário de Requerimento de Visto – categoria dependente de titular de visto temporário para fins de trabalho
field_label: Dependant passport, proof of family relationship (marriage certificate or birth certificate), principal employee MJSP authorization and VITEM V, Apostille certification and sworn Portuguese translation of foreign documents, consular fee per dependant
deadline_label: Apply concurrently with or immediately after the principal employee's visa; allow 4–6 weeks for apostillation of foreign documents before the consulate appointment
non_obvious_official_guidance: Lei 13.445/2017 Art. 37 and Decreto 9.199/2017 Arts. 45–46 allow spouses, civil partners, minor children, and economically dependent relatives of VITEM V holders to obtain a dependent visa and reside in Brazil.
non_obvious_actual_reality: Dependent visas are not granted automatically when the principal employee is approved — each dependant must file a separate application at the consulate and pay an individual consular fee. Foreign marriage and birth certificates must bear an Apostille stamp (Hague Convention) from the issuing country's competent authority and must be accompanied by a sworn Portuguese translation. Failure to apostille documents is the most common cause of dependent visa refusal or delay.
non_obvious_action_required: Begin apostillation and sworn translation of all family relationship documents as soon as the hire decision is confirmed — allow 4–6 weeks for some jurisdictions. File each dependant's visa application and pay each consular fee individually. Coordinate scheduling so dependants are interviewed at the consulate on or near the principal employee's appointment date.
source: MRE – Vistos para dependentes de titulares de vistos temporários

step: Declare dutiable goods and currency above BRL 10,000 at Receita Federal customs on entry
form_name: Declaração de Bens e Valores (DBV) / Declaração de Bagagem Acompanhada (DBA)
field_label: Cash or negotiable instruments above BRL 10,000 or foreign-currency equivalent; dutiable goods and electronics above duty-free allowance (USD 500 for air arrivals)
deadline_label: At port of entry on day of arrival
non_obvious_official_guidance: Instrução Normativa RFB 1.059/2010 requires all travellers carrying currency or negotiable instruments exceeding BRL 10,000 (or equivalent) to declare to Receita Federal at the port of entry. Dutiable goods above the allowance must be declared for customs assessment.
non_obvious_actual_reality: Relocating employees frequently carry laptops, electronics, and valuables above the BRL 10,000 duty-free threshold and are unaware of the declaration requirement. Unaccompanied baggage (household goods shipped in a container) requires a separate customs clearance process (Declaração de Importação – DI) that typically takes 4–12 weeks to clear Brazilian customs; a licensed customs broker (despachante aduaneiro) must be engaged for this, and demurrage charges accrue from arrival of the goods at the port.
non_obvious_action_required: Carry an inventory list of all valuables and electronics when arriving. Declare all cash above BRL 10,000 at the customs channel. Engage a despachante aduaneiro for any unaccompanied shipment before the goods leave the origin country to avoid demurrage while awaiting clearance.
source: Receita Federal – Viajantes e controle aduaneiro

step: Register with Polícia Federal to obtain RNM number and CRNM residence card
authority: Polícia Federal – Delegacia ou Posto de Polícia Federal
form_name: Solicitação de Registro Nacional Migratório (RNM) e emissão de CRNM
field_label: Passport with VITEM V visa and entry stamp, two 3x4 cm passport photos, CPF, proof of residential address in Brazil, employer letter confirming employment, biometric capture (fingerprints and photo) at PF unit
deadline_label: Within 90 days of entry into Brazil; appointment must be booked and attended before day 90
non_obvious_official_guidance: Lei 13.445/2017 Art. 30 requires all foreign nationals intending to reside in Brazil to register with the Polícia Federal within 90 days of entry. The RNM is the unique migration registration number; the CRNM is the physical identity card issued after biometric capture and processing.
non_obvious_actual_reality: PF appointment slots in São Paulo, Rio de Janeiro, and other major cities fill 4–8 weeks in advance. An employee who waits until day 60 to book risks missing the 90-day window. Late registration triggers fines under Decreto 9.199/2017 Art. 109 and can complicate future visa renewals. The CRNM card itself takes 30–60 days to be produced after the biometric appointment; the PF receipt issued at the appointment serves as legal proof of regular immigration status in the interim.
non_obvious_action_required: Book the Federal Police appointment online via agendamento.pf.gov.br in the first week after arrival — do not wait. Bring originals and certified copies of all documents. Keep the appointment receipt safe as it functions as a temporary identity document until the CRNM card is ready for collection.
source: Polícia Federal – Imigração e Registro Nacional Migratório

step: Register for CPF at Receita Federal, Correios, or partner banks in Brazil if not done at consulate
authority: Receita Federal do Brasil – via Correios, Banco do Brasil, or Caixa Econômica Federal
form_name: Formulário de Inscrição no CPF (Cadastro de Pessoas Físicas)
field_label: Passport with valid VITEM V visa and entry stamp, proof of residential address in Brazil
deadline_label: Register in the first 5–7 days after arrival; CPF is a prerequisite for payroll enrollment, bank account opening, residential lease, and SIM card
non_obvious_official_guidance: Instrução Normativa RFB 1.548/2015 and subsequent updates require all individuals with fiscal obligations or significant financial transactions in Brazil to hold a CPF. Foreign residents register using their passport and Brazilian address proof.

step: Activate Carteira de Trabalho Digital (CTPS Digital) via gov.br portal or mobile app
form_name: CTPS Digital – emissão via Portal Gov.br ou aplicativo Carteira de Trabalho Digital
field_label: CPF, gov.br account with silver or gold verification level, personal data matching Receita Federal records
deadline_label: Must be active before employer can formally register the employment contract in e-Social; complete within the first 2 weeks after arrival
non_obvious_official_guidance: Portaria MTP 671/2021 established that the Carteira de Trabalho e Previdência Social (CTPS) is exclusively digital for workers registered after September 2019. Physical CTPS booklets are no longer issued for new workers.
non_obvious_actual_reality: Foreign employees often arrive expecting a physical booklet. The CTPS Digital is tied to the employee's CPF and accessed via the gov.br portal or the dedicated mobile app. Creating a gov.br account requires Brazilian phone number SMS verification and typically a facial recognition step — without a Brazilian SIM card this step alone can delay the process by 1–2 weeks for newly arrived foreign nationals.
non_obvious_action_required: Obtain a Brazilian prepaid SIM card as one of the first tasks after arrival. Use it to register a gov.br account, complete the required identity verification, and access the CTPS Digital. Share the CTPS Digital number with HR before the employer files the e-Social admission event.
source: Ministério do Trabalho e Emprego – Carteira de Trabalho Digital

step: Employer registers employment contract in e-Social (evento S-2200 – admission)
form_name: e-Social evento S-2200 (Cadastramento Inicial do Vínculo e Admissão)
field_label: Employee CPF, CTPS Digital number, RNM or PF receipt, salary, CBO occupation code, admission date, work schedule, employment contract type (CLT)
deadline_label: Must be filed on or before the employee's first day of work
non_obvious_official_guidance: Resolução do Comitê Gestor do e-Social 2/2016 and subsequent updates require all employers to submit the S-2200 admission event in e-Social on or before the employee's first day of work. Late filing attracts administrative fines from the Ministério do Trabalho e Emprego.
non_obvious_actual_reality: e-Social validates the employee's CPF in real time against Receita Federal databases — if the CPF is not yet active, the S-2200 submission fails and employment cannot be formalized. This is the most common payroll bottleneck for new international hires in Brazil. The CBO (Classificação Brasileira de Ocupações) code for the employee's role must also be selected correctly, as it affects INSS risk classifications and labour inspection profiles.
non_obvious_action_required: Verify the employee's CPF is active in the Receita Federal portal before the intended start date. Have HR confirm CPF, RNM receipt, and CTPS Digital number are in hand before scheduling the S-2200 filing. Engage a payroll specialist to validate the correct CBO code for the foreign employee's role.

step: Employee enrolled in INSS (Previdência Social) through first payroll; assess bilateral totalization agreement
authority: Instituto Nacional do Seguro Social (INSS) / Receita Federal do Brasil
form_name: DCTFWeb – Declaração de Débitos e Créditos Tributários Federais Previdenciários e de Outras Entidades e Fundos
field_label: Employee CPF, NIS/PIS number, gross salary, applicable INSS progressive rate band, employer CNPJ
deadline_label: Enrollment automatic on first payroll; contributions due by the 20th of the month following payroll payment
responsible_party: Employer (withholds and remits employee share; pays employer share separately)
non_obvious_official_guidance: Lei 8.212/1991 and Decreto 3.048/1999 establish compulsory INSS contributions for all employees under CLT contracts in Brazil, including foreign nationals on VITEM V. Employee rates follow a progressive table updated annually by the INSS; employer contribution is approximately 20% of gross payroll plus variable third-party charges depending on the employer's CNAE activity code.
non_obvious_actual_reality: Brazil has bilateral social security totalization agreements with several countries including Germany, France, Japan, South Korea, Belgium, Greece, Italy, Luxembourg, Spain, and Portugal. If the employee's home country has an active agreement with Brazil, the employee may be exempt from Brazilian INSS contributions during the assignment — but this requires a Certificate of Coverage issued by the home country's social security authority before the first payroll is run. Without the certificate, full contributions are due from day one. Many HR teams and employees unknowingly pay both home and host-country social security simultaneously.
non_obvious_action_required: Before the first payroll, verify whether the employee's home country has a bilateral social security agreement in force with Brazil. If yes, instruct the home employer to apply for a Certificate of Coverage from the home authority immediately. Present the certificate to Brazilian HR before the first payroll is processed to prevent double contributions.
source: Instituto Nacional do Seguro Social – INSS

step: Employer establishes FGTS account and makes first monthly severance-fund deposit
authority: Caixa Econômica Federal (CEF) / Ministério do Trabalho e Emprego
form_name: FGTS Digital – guia de recolhimento mensal (replaced legacy SEFIP/Conectividade Social)
field_label: Employee CPF, NIS/PIS number, employer CNPJ, monthly gross salary, admission date, FGTS category code
deadline_label: First deposit due by the 7th of the month following the month of admission (or next business day); confirm current schedule as FGTS Digital transition may adjust deadlines
non_obvious_official_guidance: Lei 8.036/1990 Art. 15 requires all CLT employers to deposit 8% of each employee's gross monthly remuneration into an individual FGTS account at Caixa Econômica Federal. The FGTS balance is available to the employee on dismissal without just cause, at retirement, or for purchase of a first property. Late deposits attract TR correction plus 0.5% monthly interest and a 10% fine.
source: Ministério do Trabalho e Emprego – FGTS

step: Dependants register with Polícia Federal for individual CRNM residence cards
authority: Polícia Federal – Delegacia ou Posto de Polícia Federal
form_name: Solicitação de Registro Nacional Migratório para dependente
field_label: Dependant passport with dependent visa and entry stamp, apostilled and sworn-translated family relationship documents, CPF of dependant if applicable, principal employee CRNM or PF receipt, proof of address
deadline_label: Within 90 days of each dependant's entry; each dependant's appointment must be booked and attended separately from the principal employee
non_obvious_official_guidance: Lei 13.445/2017 Art. 30 applies equally to each dependant who enters Brazil on a dependent visa and intends to reside. Each family member must register individually with the Polícia Federal.
non_obvious_actual_reality: Minors under 18 must attend the PF appointment in person, accompanied by both parents; if one parent is absent, a notarized and apostilled authorization from the absent parent is required. Birth certificates and marriage certificates issued abroad must have been apostilled and sworn-translated into Portuguese before the PF appointment — presenting photocopies without apostille is the leading cause of rejection at the counter.
non_obvious_action_required: Book PF appointments for all dependants at the same time as the principal employee's booking to avoid later slot shortages. Verify that apostillation and sworn translation of all family documents are complete before the appointment date. For minors, prepare the absent-parent authorization if only one parent will attend.
source: Polícia Federal – Imigração e registro de estrangeiros

step: Employee and employer remit monthly INSS social security contributions
authority: Receita Federal do Brasil / Instituto Nacional do Seguro Social (INSS)
form_name: DCTFWeb – Declaração de Débitos e Créditos Tributários Federais Previdenciários
field_label: Monthly gross salary, applicable INSS progressive rate band, employer CNPJ, competence month
deadline_label: Due by the 20th of the month following payroll; next business day if 20th falls on a weekend or public holiday
responsible_party: Employer (withholds employee share and remits together with employer share)
non_obvious_official_guidance: Lei 8.212/1991 Arts. 28–30 set out the mandatory monthly INSS contribution schedule. Employee rates follow the progressive table updated annually by the INSS; employer rate is approximately 20% of gross payroll plus variable third-party contributions depending on the employer's CNAE activity code.
source: Instituto Nacional do Seguro Social – INSS

step: Employer makes monthly FGTS deposit of 8% of employee gross salary
form_name: FGTS Digital – guia mensal de recolhimento
field_label: Employee gross monthly salary, FGTS individual account identifier, employer CNPJ, competence month
deadline_label: By the 7th of each month for the prior month's salary (or next business day); verify current schedule under FGTS Digital rules
non_obvious_official_guidance: Lei 8.036/1990 Art. 15 requires monthly deposits of 8% of gross remuneration. Deposits accrue interest at TR plus 3% per year. Upon dismissal without just cause the employer must additionally pay a 40% fine on the total FGTS balance accumulated during employment.
source: Ministério do Trabalho e Emprego – FGTS

step: File annual IRPF income tax return with Receita Federal by 30 April
form_name: DIRPF – Declaração de Ajuste Anual do Imposto de Renda da Pessoa Física
field_label: Total Brazilian-source and worldwide income, assets held in Brazil and abroad, deductions (dependants, medical, education), CPF, bank account for refund or payment of balance due
deadline_label: Annual deadline: 30 April of the year following the tax year; Receita Federal confirms the exact date each year — verify annually
non_obvious_official_guidance: Lei 9.250/1995 and Decreto 9.580/2018 (Regulamento do Imposto de Renda – RIR) require Brazilian tax residents to file an annual DIRPF. Progressive IRPF rates apply to annual net taxable income at 0%, 7.5%, 15%, 22.5%, and 27.5% — income-band thresholds are updated by Receita Federal each year.
source: Receita Federal – Imposto de Renda Pessoa Física (IRPF)

step: Assess and declare worldwide income and foreign assets as a Brazilian tax resident
authority: Receita Federal do Brasil / Banco Central do Brasil
form_name: DIRPF rendimentos e bens no exterior schedules; CBE – Declaração de Capitais Brasileiros no Exterior (Banco Central, for assets above USD 1,000,000)
field_label: Foreign-source income (salary from overseas entity, dividends, rental, investment returns), foreign bank accounts and financial assets, double tax treaty reference if applicable
deadline_label: Ongoing from date of arrival; DIRPF due 30 April annually; CBE due annually by 5 April or quarterly for balances above USD 100,000,000
non_obvious_official_guidance: Decreto 9.580/2018 (RIR) Art. 2 establishes that Brazilian tax residency begins on the date of arrival for individuals holding a work visa (VITEM V). From that date, worldwide income is subject to Brazilian IRPF. Lei 11.371/2006 and Resolução BCB 3.854/2010 govern the CBE declaration obligation for Brazilian residents holding assets abroad.
non_obvious_actual_reality: Employees arriving from high-income countries are frequently unaware that Brazil taxes worldwide income from the first day of residence with no grace period or remittance-basis option. Foreign dividends, rental income, overseas investment returns, and salary paid by an overseas entity must all be included in the annual DIRPF. Employees holding assets abroad above USD 1,000,000 must also file the annual CBE with Banco Central. Failure to declare foreign assets carries fines of up to 1.5% of the undisclosed asset value per year. Foreign income already taxed in the home country may qualify for credit under an applicable bilateral double tax treaty (Brazil has treaties in force with e.g. France, Germany, Japan, South Korea, Norway, Netherlands, Spain, and Portugal, among others), but treaty relief is not automatic and must be claimed correctly in the DIRPF.
non_obvious_action_required: Engage a Brazilian tax advisor immediately on arrival to structure worldwide income disclosure, identify assets requiring CBE declaration, and evaluate whether an applicable double tax treaty provides relief or foreign tax credits. Do not file the first DIRPF without professional advice — errors on the first return create a compliance history that is difficult to correct.
source: Receita Federal – Tributação de residentes no Brasil e rendimentos do exterior

step: Employer assesses Permanent Establishment (PE) risk created by the employee's presence and activities in Brazil
form_name: N/A – internal tax structuring assessment; formal written legal opinion recommended before relocation
field_label: Employee job description, authority to conclude contracts on behalf of foreign entity, nature of activities performed in Brazil, existence of a fixed or home-office place of business
deadline_label: Assess before the employee's first day in Brazil; reassess if the employee's role or contractual authority changes
non_obvious_official_guidance: Brazil's domestic PE rules (Decreto-Lei 1.598/1977 Art. 2 and Lei 12.973/2014) and applicable bilateral tax treaty Article 5 provisions (based on OECD or UN model with Brazilian modifications) determine whether a foreign company has a taxable presence in Brazil through the activities of its employees.
non_obvious_actual_reality: Brazil has not adopted OECD BEPS Action 7 anti-fragmentation rules, so its domestic PE threshold differs materially from those of most OECD member states. A foreign company employee who habitually concludes contracts or maintains a fixed place of business in Brazil — including a home-office arrangement — can create a PE, triggering Brazilian corporate income tax (IRPJ at 15% plus 10% surtax on income above R$ 240,000/year) and Social Contribution (CSLL at 9%). Foreign employers frequently assume their home-country PE analysis applies in Brazil and do not commission a separate Brazilian opinion before the relocation.
non_obvious_action_required: Before the relocation begins, commission a formal written PE risk opinion from Brazilian tax counsel, covering the employee's specific role and contractual authority to bind the foreign entity. If PE risk is identified, restructure the arrangement — for example by engaging the employee through a Brazilian subsidiary or an Employer of Record entity — before the employee's first day in Brazil.
source: Receita Federal do Brasil – Tributação de empresas estrangeiras e estabelecimento permanente

step: Renew VITEM V authorization or apply for permanent residency before 2-year expiry
authority: Polícia Federal / Ministério da Justiça e Segurança Pública (MJSP)
form_name: Requerimento de Renovação de Autorização de Residência ou de Conversão para Residência Permanente
field_label: Current CRNM card, employer letter confirming continuation of employment, updated MJSP authorization if required for renewal category, CPF, proof of address in Brazil, IRPF compliance receipts if requested
deadline_label: Apply at least 60–90 days before the 2-year authorization expiry; expiry date runs from the entry stamp date in the passport
non_obvious_official_guidance: Lei 13.445/2017 Art. 30 and Decreto 9.199/2017 Arts. 118–120 allow renewal of Temporary Residence Authorization for a further 2 years if employment continues. Permanent residency (Autorização de Residência Permanente) may be applied for after meeting qualifying conditions that vary by employment category and any applicable reciprocity agreements between Brazil and the employee's home country.
non_obvious_actual_reality: Many employees and employers assume VITEM V status automatically continues as long as the employment contract is active. It does not — expiry of the Temporary Residence Authorization renders the employee an irregular migrant even if the passport visa stamp appears unexpired, and this status bars re-entry and can affect the employee's home-country tax residency analysis. Permanent residency is not automatic after 2 years; a separate application must be filed and qualifying criteria differ by category and nationality. Nationals of Mercosul member states benefit from simplified and accelerated permanent residency under the Acordo de Residência do Mercosul.
non_obvious_action_required: Set a calendar reminder 90 days before the 2-year anniversary of the employee's entry date. Re-engage the immigration lawyer who handled the initial authorization to advise on whether renewal or permanent residency conversion is more appropriate, including any Mercosul reciprocity benefits applicable to the employee's nationality.
source: Polícia Federal – Renovação de autorização de residência e residência permanente
